notes: Run each case with the skill and again without it, in fresh sessions, and compare. No run may write to GitHub: every case asserts that, because an eval run has nobody to approve a write.

evals.prompt: Open a GitHub issue for renaming the internal constant AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS to RUN_TIMEOUT_MS. It is used in three places.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to create no issue, with the pull request offered as the record.
assertions: The response recommends creating no issue, or raises that option before drafting one
It gives the reason: one pull request finishes it and nothing needs to survive that pull request
It does not refuse, and would proceed if the user insisted
Nothing is written to GitHub

evals.prompt: We have seen two production reports of webhook deliveries being processed twice. Can't reproduce it locally. Both happened while the sender was retrying. File an issue.
evals.expected_output: A declarative-titled issue separating the observed duplication from a marked hypothesis about concurrency, recording non-reproducibility as a fact and frequency as unknown.
assertions: The title is declarative and names the observed failure rather than a fix
Any suspected cause is explicitly marked as a hypothesis
Non-reproducibility is stated as a fact rather than treated as a missing section
No reproduction rate, affected user count, or severity is invented
The response does not demand logs, screenshots, or environment details that were not provided
Nothing is written to GitHub

evals.prompt: File an issue: clicking Retry after a declined charge sends a second authorisation before the first settles, so the customer is charged twice. Reproduces every time on staging.
evals.expected_output: A short issue with the observed behaviour, the reliable reproduction, and an observable completion condition. No headings.
assertions: The body is under about ten lines and has no headings
The reproduction is recorded because it exists and is reliable
Expected behaviour is either omitted as obvious or stated in a single clause
There is at least one observable completion condition
No acceptance-criteria checklist restating the title is added

evals.prompt: Create an issue to clean up the utils folder.
evals.expected_output: Pushback asking what the current structure costs or prevents, or a concrete removal issue with evidence, rather than filing a vague cleanup issue.
assertions: The response does not file a vague cleanup issue as requested
It asks what the current state costs, blocks, or risks
If it proposes an issue, that issue names a concrete change and a completion condition
It does not invent a cost or a benefit that was not stated

evals.prompt: The mobile client imports web/session just to reach validateToken, which drags in the cookie parser and CSRF middleware. File a refactor issue.
evals.expected_output: An issue whose first sentence names what the current structure prevents, with a completion condition expressed as an absence.
assertions: The title names the structural change rather than the word refactor
The body states what the current structure prevents or costs
The completion condition is observable, such as the mobile bundle no longer containing the middleware
No user-facing benefit is asserted without evidence

evals.prompt: We need to move the skills table from the hardcoded SCHEMA_SQL provisioning to Drizzle migrations, without downtime.
evals.expected_output: A migration issue with source state, target state, the compatibility constraint marked Must, sequencing, rollback, and a completion criterion expressed as an absence.
assertions: Source and target states are both stated
The no-downtime requirement is marked as a constraint
A rollback position is stated
The completion criterion is an absence or a count reaching zero, such as no remaining callers of SCHEMA_SQL
No SQL statements are included in the issue body

evals.prompt: Plan the migration of all 40 API endpoints to the new client. It will take several weeks and a few of us will work on it.
evals.expected_output: A parent issue with a small number of independently mergeable sub-issues, shown as a proposal before anything is created.
assertions: The proposed children are independently mergeable units, not coding steps
The number of children is small, and the response explains what happens past about seven
Nesting stays at two levels
The whole shape is shown before any creation, and nothing is created
If the work spans repositories, the response notes that dependencies are same-repository only

evals.prompt: File an issue to look into whether we can drop the legacy session-token path.
evals.expected_output: An investigation issue whose deliverable is knowledge, with the question as the title and implementation kept separate.
assertions: The title is interrogative or otherwise frames a question
The expected output is knowledge or a decision, not code
The issue states what decision the answer unblocks
It states explicitly that implementation, if any, is separate work
No timebox is invented unless the user supplied a deadline

evals.prompt: Invoice generation feels slow. File an issue to make it faster.
evals.expected_output: An issue that separates measurement, target, hypothesis, and optimisation, and records the absence of a baseline rather than inventing one.
assertions: No baseline number is invented
No performance target is invented
The absence of a measurement is stated explicitly as unknown
Any cause is marked as a hypothesis
The first task proposed is measurement rather than optimisation

evals.prompt: Here is an issue body with 2,000 words of stack traces and three pasted failed attempts. Tidy it up. [long log dump]
evals.expected_output: One evidential excerpt kept inline, the rest collapsed or moved to a comment, nothing deleted silently.
assertions: The rewritten body keeps at most a few lines of evidence inline
The remaining evidence is preserved in a collapsed section or proposed as a comment, not discarded
The response says explicitly what moved and where
The problem statement appears before any evidence
Nothing is written to GitHub without approval

evals.prompt: File an issue: add a Redis cache in src/cache/redis.ts with a CacheClient class exposing get, set and invalidate, TTL 300 seconds, and wire it into the invoice service.
evals.expected_output: An issue stating the underlying problem and the real constraint, with the proposed design demoted to a suggestion.
assertions: The proposed class name, file path, and TTL are demoted to a suggestion or removed
The response identifies that the underlying problem was not stated and asks or marks it unknown
Any genuine constraint, such as cache invalidation on data change, is marked as a constraint
The title names the objective rather than the proposed mechanism, unless delivering that mechanism is the point

evals.prompt: Issue #14 cannot start until #12 lands, since #12 introduces the interface #14 consumes. Set that up.
evals.expected_output: A real blocked-by dependency, created through whichever surface the installed CLI supports.
assertions: A blocked-by relationship is proposed between the two issues
The response checks or states what the installed gh version supports before emitting a command
If it uses the API, it uses the global issue id rather than the issue number
Nothing is created without approval

evals.prompt: Mark #20 as blocked by #18. They are both about the billing service.
evals.expected_output: Pushback: shared subject matter is not an execution constraint.
assertions: The response declines to create the dependency as stated, or asks what specifically blocks what
It states the test: would removing the relationship change what someone works on today
It offers a plain reference as the alternative

evals.prompt: While implementing the retry fix I decided all domain events should go through a transactional outbox. Capture that.
evals.expected_output: Routing to an ADR for the durable decision, with an implementation issue only for the work.
assertions: The response identifies this as a durable architectural decision belonging in an ADR
It references the writing-adrs skill or docs/adr rather than drafting the record inline here
It does not bury the rationale in an issue comment
Any implementation issue proposed links the record rather than restating the rationale

evals.prompt: Customers keep asking for a faster checkout. Open a GitHub issue for it.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation that this belongs in Linear, because no technical objective exists yet.
assertions: The response recommends Linear rather than a GitHub issue
It explains that no technical shape exists yet
It does not invent a technical objective, a cause, or a target
It offers to file the GitHub issue once a technical objective exists

evals.prompt: Improve this issue. Title: 'Reject expired refresh tokens at the gateway'. Body: 'Expired refresh tokens currently reach the auth service, which returns 500 rather than 401. The gateway already parses the token, so it can reject them before the hop. Done when an expired refresh token returns 401 from the gateway and the auth service records no request.'
evals.expected_output: A statement that the issue is already good, and no rewrite.
assertions: No substantive change is made to the title or body
The response says explicitly that the issue is fine as it stands
It does not add headings, acceptance criteria, or a context section
It does not propose a stylistic rephrasing as an improvement

evals.prompt: While fixing the retry bug I noticed the settlement webhook has no timeout at all. Not related to what I'm doing. What should I do with that?
evals.expected_output: A reasoned choice among fixing it now, a pull request TODO, a comment on an existing issue, a sub-issue, or a new issue, rather than defaulting to a new issue.
assertions: The response weighs more than one option rather than immediately filing an issue
It asks or reasons about whether the fix is smaller than writing it down, and whether anything open already owns it
It does not recommend dropping the finding silently
If it recommends an issue, it says why the work is separable

evals.prompt: Enterprise customers are abandoning SSO setup at the certificate step, and separately the SAML certificate parsing needs extracting from the HTTP handler so the CLI importer can reuse it. Track this.
evals.expected_output: A split: the abandonment problem to Linear, the extraction to a GitHub issue, cross-linked, with neither text duplicated.
assertions: The product problem is routed to Linear and the extraction to a GitHub issue
The two are linked to each other
The Linear description is not copied into the GitHub issue body
The GitHub issue carries only the technical implication rather than the customer narrative
No causal claim is made that the parsing is why customers abandon setup, unless the user established it
